title: Rust: Process and Signals
description: Use std::process to run external commands and handle process interaction.

steps.title: Run a Shell Command
steps.description: Use `std::process::Command::new` to run `echo "Hello from Rust!"` and capture output. Print the stdout.

verification.failureMessage: Run echo "Hello from Rust!" and capture its output.

steps.title: Pipe Data Between Processes
steps.description: Pipe echo output into a command. Run `echo "hello world" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'` by chaining commands. Print the uppercase result.
hints: Pass the full pipeline as one argument.

verification.failureMessage: Run a pipeline that uppercases 'hello world'.

steps.title: Process Exit Status
steps.description: Run commands that succeed (exit 0) and fail (exit 1). Use `.status()` to get the exit code. Print success or failure for each.
hints: `.status()` waits for the process and returns ExitStatus.

verification.failureMessage: Run true and false commands and print their exit status.

steps.title: Environment Variables
steps.description: Set and get environment variables for a subprocess. Run a command that reads env vars and prints them.
hints: `.env(key, val)` sets an env var for the subprocess.

verification.failureMessage: Set GREETING env var and print 'Hello world'.

steps.title: Timeout Process Execution
steps.description: Spawn a long-running command and kill it after a timeout. Use `std::time::Duration` and `thread::sleep` to simulate timeout logic.
hints: Sleep for a duration, then `kill()` the child process.

verification.failureMessage: Spawn a long process and kill it after a timeout.
